findings.evidence: `ChevalleyRelations.lean:66-99` contains only `commute_rootSubgroupPoints` (hypotheses `hjk : j ≠ k`, `hli : l ≠ i`) and the single orientation `⁅x_ij(c), x_jl(d)⁆ = x_il(cd)`; `grep -rn "commutatorElement" TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Transvection.lean` shows no reversed-orientation lemma either. `Mathlib/GroupTheory/Commutator/Basic.lean:66` supplies `commutatorElement_inv : ⁅g₁, g₂⁆⁻¹ = ⁅g₂, g₁⁆`, and `rootSubgroupPoints` is a `MonoidHom` (RootSubgroup.lean:85), so the derivation is immediate.
findings.fix: Add the reverse orientation, e.g. `⁅rootSubgroupPoints hjl g, rootSubgroupPoints hij f⁆ = (rootSubgroupPoints hil (AdditiveGroup.gaPointMul f g))⁻¹`, proved in two lines by `rw [← commutatorElement_inv, commutatorElement_rootSubgroupPoints, ← map_inv]`.
findings.issue: For two index pairs `(i,j)`, `(k,l)` there are three in-scope configurations: non-chaining (covered by `commute_rootSubgroupPoints`), `j = k` (covered here, constant `+1`), and `l = i` (constant `-1`) — the last is covered by neither theorem, since `commute_rootSubgroupPoints` requires `hli : l ≠ i`. The PR description claims "both orientations of the three-index type-A commutator relation (including the `-1` structure constant)" are proved; only one is.

summary: Hypotheses and typeclass levels of both new theorems are minimal and match the matrix lemmas they transport. However the commutator relation is proved for only one of the two chaining orientations, leaving the `l = i` configuration covered by neither new theorem, despite the PR description claiming both.
